notes: Semgrep p/smart-contracts produced 54 findings, all INFO severity (performance/best-practice: use-custom-error, prefix-increment, short-revert-string, ownable2step, etc.) -> all discarded per Informational->discard rule. The only security-adjacent one, use-ownable2step, is a known centralization design decision (owner trusted, KI#8) and duplicates Aderyn centralization-risk.
All 9 Slither divide-before-multiply + 1 incorrect-exp + 1 too-many-digits hits are in lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol (OOS dependency, OOS root cause) -> dropped.
Slither missing-zero-check, Aderyn state-no-address-check, push-zero-opcode, unspecific-solidity-pragma, modifier-used-only-once -> QA/noise per filter list, dropped.
Slither missing-inheritance (StableStaker should inherit IStableStaker) -> Informational, dropped.

Timestamp/block-dependency findings RETAINED per suite rule (time-driven reward accrual is load-bearing), but assessed as tool-noise: all are standard MasterChef _updatePool elapsed-time accrual or non-timestamp comparisons Slither mislabels; no manipulable window.

findings.description: State written after external strategy call: initiateMigration calls _routeExit (strategy.withdraw/relinquishPrincipal) then post-checks strategy.principalOf and writes poolState=Migrating, yieldStrategy=0, migrationInfo. Slither flags same as reentrancy-no-eth at L417.
findings.assessment: LIKELY NOISE. Function is nonReentrant + onlyMigrator (trusted permissioned role). External callee is the configured yield strategy (reflax-yield-vault, in-ecosystem). Reentrancy is blocked by the guard; the post-call writes are intentional CEI-relaxed migration bookkeeping. Worth a manual glance at strategy-callback trust boundary but not a standalone exploit.

findings.description: Reentrancy: _routeExit (strategy.relinquishPrincipal/withdraw) and strategy.deposit external calls precede yieldStrategy[token]/allowance state writes; YieldStrategySet emitted after. Aderyn unchecked-return at L241/L258 overlaps.
findings.assessment: WORTH A LOOK. This is the ONE state-mutating principal-moving path WITHOUT a nonReentrant guard (onlyOwner only). Calls old strategy (drain) then new strategy (deposit) with state writes interleaved (yieldStrategy[token]=strategy at L248 sits between the drain and the sweep-deposit). Owner is trusted (Law 3) and strategies are in-ecosystem, so practical risk is low, but the missing guard + interleaved write on a strategy-swap is the most interesting static signal here -> flag for code-scanner (yield-strategy external-call + state-machine).

findings.description: Reentrancy: _settle (phUSD.mint) and _routeDeposit (strategy.deposit) external calls before user.amount/pool.totalStaked/rewardDebt writes and _stakers.add.
findings.assessment: LIKELY NOISE. nonReentrant + whenNotPaused. phUSD.mint is the trusted in-ecosystem reward token; strategy.deposit is the configured strategy. Standard MasterChef settle-then-credit ordering under a guard.

findings.description: Reentrancy: _settle (phUSD.mint) and _routeDeposit (strategy.deposit) external calls before position-accounting writes and _stakers.add. Migrator-only deposit path on the new staker.
findings.assessment: LIKELY NOISE. nonReentrant + onlyMigrator (trusted role). Mirrors stake ordering; reentrancy guarded.

findings.description: Return value of strategy.deposit(token, idleBalance, address(this)) ignored at L258 (sweep of idle balance into new strategy). Aderyn unchecked-return corroborates (L258).
findings.assessment: WORTH A LOOK. Unlike stake/withdraw which capture _routeDeposit/_routeExit deltas, the setYieldStrategy idle-sweep discards strategy.deposit's booked-principal return. If a strategy haircuts on deposit (market/ERC4626 rounding, per CLAUDE.md), the swept balance's booked principal can diverge from internal totalStaked, desyncing principalOf vs poolInfo.totalStaked. Flag for code-scanner: accounting-desync on strategy adoption/swap. (Other unused-return hits at L297/317/357/529/627 are EnumerableSet add/remove -> intentional, noise.)

findings.description: Return value of EnumerableSet add()/remove() ignored at L297 (stake), L317 (withdraw), L357 (emergencyWithdraw), L529 (_exitPosition), L627 (depositFor). Aderyn unchecked-return corroborates.
findings.assessment: NOISE. Intentional idempotent set membership management (add returns false if present, remove false if absent); the bool is not actionable here. QA at most.

findings.description: Local accumulators total (L64) and migratedCount (L75) in migrate, and total (L491) in StableStaker.batchMigrate, declared without explicit initialization. Aderyn uninitialized-local-variable corroborates StableStakerMigrator L75.
findings.assessment: NOISE. uint256 default-zero accumulators incremented in a loop; correct by Solidity semantics. False positive.

findings.description: External call newStaker.depositFor inside the user loop (migrate, L78); StableStaker._exitPosition has phUSD.mint inside the batchMigrate loop (L532). Aderyn costly-loop corroborates StableStaker L492.
findings.assessment: LOW / DESIGN. Per-user external calls in batch migration are inherent to the batched-migrate design; gas-griefing/partial-batch DoS is a known operational concern (batches built off-chain via getStakersRange). Note for code-scanner state-machine review but not a static-only finding; severity Low.

findings.description: block.timestamp used in comparisons: _updatePool (L705/L714 elapsed accrual), pendingReward (L639), _routeExit (L775, actually a balanceOf compare mislabeled), finalizeAndReset (L588, actually a totalStaked==0 compare mislabeled). RETAINED per time-driven-suite rule.
findings.assessment: RETAINED-BUT-NOISE. Reward accrual is genuinely time-driven (elapsed * phusdPerSecond), but there is no attacker-controllable window: emission is linear in real elapsed time, dust rounds down, empty-pool windows accrue nothing (KI#1/#2). The _routeExit (L775) and finalizeAndReset (L588) hits are balance/totalStaked comparisons Slither misattributes to timestamp. No miner-timestamp manipulation lever. Kept visible for severity-classifier per suite policy.
